requirements.source: 10.1.5.1 p3 and Table 10.2 numeric rows; J3/24-007 PDF p175.
requirements.definition: A numeric intrinsic operation is an intrinsic operation whose intrinsic-operator is +, -, *, /, or **. The operator in such an operation is a numeric intrinsic operator.
requirements.oracle:

S10.1.5.1-003 numeric-operator classification runtime fixtures: five complete run/effect/f2023 programs exercise +, binary -, *, /, and ** on INTEGER operands with hand-computed literal results: 14+(-5)=9, 14-(-5)=19, (-6)*7=-42, 17/5=3 by integer division, and 2**5=32. Operands are selected so the plausible wrong numeric operator alternatives do not produce the same value; the division guard compares the expression directly so a real-division interpretation would produce 3.4 and fail rather than being hidden by integer assignment.

requirements.title: Character intrinsic operations are same-kind character concatenations
requirements.definition: The character intrinsic operation is the intrinsic operation whose intrinsic-operator is // and whose two operands are of type character with the same kind type parameter. The operator in that operation is the character intrinsic operator, and Table 10.2 gives a character result.

S10.1.5.1-005 logical-operator classification runtime fixtures: five complete run/effect/f2023 programs exercise .NOT., .AND., .OR., .EQV., and .NEQV. with literal LOGICAL operands and branch-only observations of the result. .NOT. checks both .FALSE. -> .TRUE. and .TRUE. -> .FALSE. requirements.title: Relational intrinsic operations cover numeric, character, enumeration, and enum operand families
requirements.definition: The relational intrinsic operators are .EQ., .NE., .GT., .GE., .LT., .LE., ==, /=, >, >=, <, and <=. A relational intrinsic operation uses one of those operators. Numeric relational operations have numeric operands; character relational operations have character operands whose kind type parameters shall be the same; enumeration relational operations have operands of the same enumeration type; enum relational operations have one enum operand and the other operand of the same enum type or an integer expression involving an enumerator of that type. Table 10.2 gives logical results and the admitted equality and ordering families.
